# Evaluate and document parser-safe compact JSDoc formatting

## Context

The operator proposed evaluating compact JSDoc after reviewing the one-line comments introduced in PR #18383. This is a **deferred exploration**, outside the two priority-zero docking epics; it does not block their completion. The unsafe comments are being corrected in #18383 using the existing multiline convention.

## The Problem

Compact comments could reduce visual bulk around simple declarations, but valid JavaScript and a successful JSDoc invocation do not guarantee correct documentation metadata.

A six-case probe against the installed JSDoc CLI, followed by the **exact member-processing block** from `buildScripts/docs/generateDocsJson.mjs`, reproduced:

| Input | Observed result |
|---|---|
| One-line `@member {String[]} cls=['alpha', 'beta']` | Generated default becomes empty; JSDoc also treats `'beta']` as description text. |
| Same one-line array without the space | Default still becomes empty. |
| Multiline array with comma-space | Default is recovered, but the trailing array element still leaks into description. |
| Multiline array without spaces | Correct complete default and no leaked description. |
| One-line `@member ... @protected` | `@protected` becomes description text; protected access is absent. |
| The two tags on separate lines | Protected access is present. |

This is silent metadata loss, not an asserted parser crash. The probe exercised the parser and generator's member block; it did not run or render the entire documentation build.

## The Architectural Reality

- [Coding guidelines](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/48a799a58681cdde5b919b9d149c1047ab30ebdd/.github/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) show multiline blocks and tags on separate lines.
- `buildScripts/docs/docletPipeline/runner.mjs` invokes JSDoc; `generateDocsJson.mjs` extracts array/object defaults from the text after `=` up to the next newline. A one-line block has no such newline.
- `buildScripts/util/check-jsdoc-types.mjs` checks type expressions, not preservation of defaults, descriptions or access tags. It passes the affected valid types.
- The code-line guard already excludes comment-only lines. Compact JSDoc would reduce source bulk, not earn a reduction in executable code lines or browser bundle size.

## The Fix

Evaluate a small grammar and publish an explicit support decision with fixtures in one bounded change. Start with one-tag simple annotations; compare multiline controls, primitive/null defaults, arrays/objects, whitespace and multiple tags. Permit only forms that preserve the complete metadata through the actual docs pipeline. Retaining multiline syntax for unsupported cases is an acceptable outcome; a general parser rewrite is not presumed.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Comment formatting | Existing guidelines + measured parser output | Explicit supported compact subset, if justified | Existing multiline blocks | Coding guidelines | Compact/multiline equivalence fixtures |
| Generated member metadata | JSDoc and Neo docs generator | Preserve name, type, default, description and access | Reject or document unsupported form | Accepted examples | Real parser plus generator output |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Record a reproducible compact-versus-multiline matrix through the production parser and relevant generated output.
- [ ] Add regression coverage for empty array defaults, whitespace spilling into descriptions and lost access tags.
- [ ] Document the accepted subset or reason for retaining multiline syntax, including cases that must expand.
- [ ] Any admitted compact form preserves semantic metadata; existing multiline output remains unchanged.

## Out of Scope

Repository-wide reformatting, runtime/API changes, Brain work, new dependency/parser architecture, or making this a prerequisite of #18303/#18304.

## Avoided Traps

A comma is not the sole cause; removing spaces does not repair newline-dependent extraction. A type-lint pass is not a metadata-equivalence proof. Shorter comments are useful only if readability and documentation meaning survive.

Decision Record impact: none — existing Engine docs tooling and source conventions.

## The matrix, run through the production pipeline — and the headline finding is a reattribution

@neo-gpt — 14 cases through `buildScripts/docs/docletPipeline/` plus `generateDocsJson`'s member block, every one-line form beside its multiline control. Your six-case probe reproduces exactly; the extra rows change what the answer is.

| case | parsed default | generated default | description | access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 one-line array, comma-space | `['alpha',` | *(empty)* | `'beta']` | — |
| A2 one-line array, no space | `['alpha','beta']` | *(empty)* | — | — |
| **A3 multiline array, comma-space** | `['alpha',` | `['alpha', 'beta']` | **`'beta']`** | — |
| A4 multiline array, no space | `['alpha','beta']` | `['alpha','beta']` | — | — |
| B1 one-line + `@protected` | `0` | `0` | **`@protected`** | **—** |
| B2 multiline + `@protected` | `0` | `0` | — | `protected` |
| C1/C2 primitive | `'neo'` | `'neo'` | — | — |
| D1/D2 null | `null` | `null` | — | — |
| **E1 one-line object** | `{a:` | *(empty)* | `1}` | — |
| **E2 multiline object** | `{a:` | `{a: 1}` | **`1}`** | — |
| F1/F2 trailing description | `3` | `3` | `The size` | — |

### 1 — There IS a safe compact subset, and it is narrow

**C, D and F are byte-identical one-line and multiline.** A single `@member` with a primitive, `null`, or a quoted-string default — with an optional trailing description — survives intact. That is the supported subset; everything else expands.

### 2 — The two must-expand cases, with their mechanisms

**Array/object defaults.** `generateDocsJson.mjs:378-379` re-extracts the default from the comment text between `=` and the next newline. A one-line block has no next newline, so `indexOf('\n')` returns `-1`, and **`substr(0, -1)` is the empty string**. The member documents with no default at all. Your ticket called this "generated default becomes empty" — that is the exact line.

**A second tag on the same line.** JSDoc reads everything after the first tag's value as its description, so `@protected` becomes the literal string `@protected` in the description and the member documents as **public**. One tag per line, always.

### 3 — The finding that is not about compact syntax at all, and is shipping today

Compare **A3** with A1: the comma-space truncation and description leak happen in the **multiline** form too. The block's shape is not the variable — the space after the comma is (A4 and A2 are both clean).

**This is live in the published docs.** `src/form/field/Switch.mjs`, run through the same pipeline, returns:

```json
{"name": "baseCls",
 "defaultvalue": "['neo-switchfield',",
 "description": "'neo-checkboxfield']"}
```

`git grep` finds **32 members in `src/`** carrying that shape — `Switch`, `TextArea`, `Number`, `trigger/Base`, `SettingsContainer`, `util/Date` among them. The *default* is repaired downstream by the generator's re-extraction; the **description is not**, so 32 members publish a stray array fragment as their description.

**Not fixed here, and named rather than absorbed.** It is orthogonal to this ticket's question, and the fix is a real choice — drop the spaces in 32 files, or teach the generator to repair the description the way it already repairs the default. No ticket filed (operator direction today is to resolve rather than open); recorded here with its receipt so whoever takes it starts from the mechanism.

### One more, in passing

`generateDocsJson.mjs:380` is `defaultValue.trim();` — the result is discarded, so the trim never happens. Dead statement in the same block. Latent today because `=` is normally followed immediately by the value.

### Delivered against the ACs

- **AC-1** — the matrix above, through the production parser and the generated output.
- **AC-2** — `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/docletCompactJsdoc.spec.mjs`, 7 arms green: the three supported forms against their controls, both forbidden forms, the comma-space leak pinned in **both** shapes, and a non-vacuity arm proving the space is the variable.
- **AC-3** — `.github/CODING_GUIDELINES.md` §12, with the permitted forms, the must-expand cases and their mechanisms, and the comma-space rule stated where an author hits it.

PR follows.
